source.title: An Investigation Into the Stochasticity of Batch Whitening
source.authors: Lei Huang; Lei Zhao; Yi Zhou; Fan Zhu; Li Liu; Ling Shao

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; figure values are not recoverable as text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains a VGG network on CIFAR-10 and reports training-error outcomes for batch-normalization and batch-whitening variants. This bears on training-error behavior, though it does not test the claim’s random-label or size-scaling conditions.
record.gate_note: The VGG CIFAR-10 training-error plot is figure-only. The authors explicitly state that PCA fails to train, ZCA-16 trains well, other ZCA configurations fail from numerical instability, and ItN works best. Other cited studies’ results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The VGG CIFAR-10 experiments directly report training classification error and explicit training failures under SGD, bearing on V1 under different normalization recipes. They do not compare BN with an otherwise identical unnormalized network, so they do not test V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute differing whitening optimization behavior to introduced stochasticity and argue for controlling its magnitude. They also conclude that covariance-based population-statistic estimation is more stable, and that whitening can improve GAN performance while sacrificing training stability.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares batch whitening transformations and BN in a VGG CIFAR-10 training experiment, rather than testing the claim’s SGD/Adam size, label-corruption, and near-zero-error recipe directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Whitening transformation and group size affect training behavior; PCA fails across configurations, most ZCA configurations are numerically unstable, and ZCA-16 and ItN train successfully.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, full ZCA whitening trains worse than BN, while group-16 ZCA and CD train better than BN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whitening's effect on training speed depends on the transformation and group size; this comparison does not establish BN's advantage over no normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Whitening transformations differ in stochastic normalization disturbance, ImageNet validation accuracy, GAN FID/IS, and sensitivity to hyperparameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Controlling whitening stochasticity affects optimization and predictive or generative performance; these measures do not establish any additional claim version.

record.problems: Training-error values in Figure 7 are figure-only in the supplied text. No numerical training-error values or uncertainty estimates are provided for this comparison.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, model-size scaling, early stopping, Adam classification training, and comparisons of regularization recipes. Random initialization is not explicitly documented here; near-zero error in successful runs is unreadable.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and benefits of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, matched plain versus residual networks, and the special initialization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Initial stability thresholds, loss-curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability training.
BN versus matched networks without normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No support verdict is justified for successful VGG runs because their near-zero training-error endpoints cannot be established from the supplied text. Whitening-specific failures qualify recipe scope rather than establish failure of the original training recipes. The ImageNet results report validation accuracy, and the GAN experiments report generation quality and hyperparameter sensitivity, rather than the outcomes named by V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, model-size comparisons, early stopping, Adam, and regularized recipes.
